inputs.userGoal: 1. I am the product owner (Ray Swan) for the manifest. 2. I don't have a cost center, so we can use a default that is allowed. 3. bootstrap should include github reposity/environment creation as an external prerequisite (part of the actions in this work).
subGoals: Dev-only clean-room bootstrap with no Test or Prod changes.
Security-first workload federation with no client secret and no subscription-scoped deployment role.
Reuse the approved same-subscription backend account while isolating R1 state in a dedicated container.

reasoning.whyChosen: The exact repository is part of the approved product identity and is required before GitHub environment federation can be proven.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Creates a separate repository boundary and later requires an explicit generated-source push approval.

resources.name: github-rubyrayjuntos-azure-aiml-ops-environment-dev

reasoning.whyChosen: Generated workflows declare environment dev, and the approved federated subject uses the environment claim.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Keeps federation stable across protected branches, but the current private-repository billing plan cannot enforce required reviewers. The dev_manual policy remains an unresolved release gate.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The protected environment belongs to the new repository.

reasoning.whyChosen: The generated R1 repository requires an administrator-created, environment-isolated resource group and must not require subscription Owner.
alternativesConsidered: Let generated Terraform create its own resource group
reasoning.tradeoffs: Adds one bootstrap resource but provides clean ownership, cost, RBAC, and rollback boundaries.

resources.name: rg-azmlops-0001dev-tf
resources.subtype: Existing shared Terraform backend resource group

reasoning.whyChosen: The user approved reuse of the discovered same-subscription backend boundary.
alternativesConsidered: Create a separate backend resource group
reasoning.tradeoffs: Retains a legacy-named shared prerequisite while avoiding another storage account and cross-subscription authorization.

resources.name: stazmlops0001devtf

reasoning.whyChosen: Read-only discovery verified same-subscription placement, East US location, Entra blob access, and disabled Shared Key.
alternativesConsidered: Create a dedicated R1 storage account
reasoning.tradeoffs: Reuses an existing backend account; isolation is provided at container and state-key boundaries instead of account level.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The existing storage account is contained by the approved backend resource group.

resources.name: azure-ai-ml-ops-r1

reasoning.whyChosen: A dedicated private container separates R1 state from the legacy default container without changing the approved storage account.
alternativesConsidered: Reuse the default container with a unique key
reasoning.tradeoffs: Adds one low-cost bootstrap object and an explicit RBAC scope, while avoiding state/audit ambiguity.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The container is created in the existing shared backend account.

reasoning.whyChosen: A new application prevents reuse of the legacy subscription-Owner principal and gives the generated repository an auditable identity boundary.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Creates one additional tenant object but avoids secrets, legacy subjects, and excessive cross-environment access.

references.title: Register an application with Microsoft Entra ID

resources.name: sp-gh-azure-ai-ml-ops-r1-dev-oidc
resources.subtype: Enterprise application for the GitHub deployment identity

reasoning.whyChosen: Azure RBAC assignments target the service-principal object ID associated with the approved application client ID.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Requires correlation of application/client and principal/object IDs in the bootstrap receipt.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The service principal instantiates the new application in the tenant.

resources.name: github-azure-aiml-ops-dev-environment

reasoning.whyChosen: The generated workflows declare the protected dev environment, so the environment subject is exact and stable across approved branches.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Authentication depends on the repository environment being present and correctly referenced by every deployment job.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The credential belongs to the application and must match the created GitHub environment exactly.

references.title: Create a workload identity federation trust

resources.name: ra-azure-ai-ml-ops-r1-backend-data-contributor

reasoning.whyChosen: Terraform backend initialization needs Entra-authorized blob read/write/delete and lease operations, scoped only to the dedicated R1 container.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Container scope minimizes blast radius but requires the container to exist before the assignment.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Both the target container and service-principal object ID must exist.

resources.name: ra-azure-ai-ml-ops-r1-dev-contributor

reasoning.whyChosen: Generated Terraform must manage R1 Dev workload resources inside the administrator-owned environment boundary.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Resource-group Contributor is broader than future per-resource roles but is bounded to one Dev environment and cannot assign roles.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The environment scope and deployment principal must exist before assignment.

resources.name: ra-azure-ai-ml-ops-r1-dev-user-access-administrator

properties.purpose: Generated Terraform creates the project evidence-container data-role assignment.
properties.futureHardening: Replace with a conditioned RBAC role when the R1 provider contract supports it.

reasoning.whyChosen: The current R1 contract explicitly requires environment-scoped User Access Administrator for generated evidence role assignment creation.
alternativesConsidered: Role Based Access Control Administrator with an ABAC condition
reasoning.tradeoffs: This is a privileged role. Scoping it to one Dev resource group satisfies the current contract, while a conditioned role is the preferred later hardening path.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The environment scope and deployment principal must exist before assignment.

overallReasoning.summary: Bootstrap only the administrator-owned prerequisites required to generate and later plan the Azure AI ML Ops R1 Dev repository.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: The existing storage account is reused to minimize cost and preserve the shared-backend ownership boundary, while a dedicated container prevents state collision. Public networking, private endpoints, disaster recovery, application monitoring, and Azure ML resources are intentionally outside this bootstrap; generated project Terraform owns the Azure ML workload after a separate plan approval. GitHub repository and environment operations are external prerequisites rather than Azure ARM resources.

plan.validation: Deployed and independently verified: the private GitHub repository and Dev environment exist; four identifier-only environment secrets are present; the Dev resource group succeeded; the backend container is private; Shared Key and blob public access remain disabled; the single-tenant application, service principal, and exact environment-scoped federated credential agree; role assignments are limited to container Storage Blob Data Contributor and Dev-resource-group Contributor plus User Access Administrator; no Owner assignment exists; and the post-apply Terraform plan returned no changes. Required-reviewer protection is unsupported by the current GitHub billing plan, so protected-branch policy is active and dev_manual enforcement remains an unresolved release gate.
architecturePrinciples: One resource has one declared owner.
Use Entra workload federation and avoid stored credentials.
Assign Azure roles at the narrowest R1-compatible scope.
Keep mutation, planning, and deployment approval gates separate.
